text:
sophia: heads-up — after landing tokenizer micro-optim (PR#4321) we see host p99 go up ~20% on small requests, repro in prod canary :eyes:

mike: any flamegraphs or perf snaps?

sophia: attaching quick paste of perf-summary from the hot hostbox (snipped):
```
top functions by CPU:
  parse_and_tokenize()        34.1%
  http2_writev()              12.3%
  stream_chunk_coalesce()      9.8%
  kv_cache::lookup_path()      8.5%
  grpc_unmarshal()             5.6%
```

kevin: hmm kv_cache shows more work than usual — misses spiked? timeline aligns with tokenizer change?

olivia: I ran a quick microbench on the same host image + saved kernel-selection logs: new tokenizer added extra memcpy in parse path, forcing slower kernel for short sequences.

mike: can you paste the kernel decision lines? that would confirm selector threshold bump.

olivia: snippet below from /var/log/redwood/kernelselect.log (shortened):
```
[1728456701] seq_len=12 features=0x3 set kernel=general_scalar
[1728456701] seq_len=64 features=0x3 set kernel=vector_fast
[1728456760] seq_len=12 features=0x7 set kernel=general_scalar  # after tokenizer change
```

sophia: so tokenizer change increased work in the host parse (extra tokens emitted?) -> selector picks scalar kernel more often -> p99 regress.

kevin: also worth noting stream_chunk_coalesce() cost rose — looks like HTTP framing producing more, smaller chunks. grpc write threads doing more syscalls.

mike: any quick experiments to validate? toggle tokenizer to previous branch? or force kernel hint?

olivia: I did a canary where I set env REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=vector_fast for the service; p99 dropped back ~12% but overall throughput slightly worse for very long seqs (expected).

sophia: good repro. plan A: roll back micro-alloc in tokenizer (very targeted) and add unit to ensure no extra memcpy; plan B: update kernelselector thresholds + add short-seq fastpath.

mike: also add a batching heuristic tweak: bump minibatch trigger to 8ms for small requests to let coalesce gather more tokens. should reduce syscall churn.

kevin: KV cache: misses correlate with these small requests — I suspect key normalization changed slightly (strip vs no-strip). check tokenizer normalization diff in PR#4321.

olivia: confirmed: we started lowercasing earlier which changes prefix keys. PR#4321 had that line. reverting normalization gets kv-hit-rate back to 98% from 83%.

sophia: ok that explains two vectors: kernel choose via seq length/features and kv miss causing extra backend lookup. both multiply latency.

deploy-bot: Canary service/redwood-host-23: rollback triggered by perf-alert (rule: host-p99 > 15% baseline). :warning:

mike: action items:
- revert normalization change from PR#4321 (olivia)
- add test that asserts kv-hit-rate >= 95% on short prompt set (kevin)
- add kernel-selector unit + telemetry for seq_len distribution (sophia)
- tweak batching heuristic in patch branch and run microbench (mike)

olivia: already opened PR#4334 to revert normalization, running canary now.

kevin: I'll draft the kv-hit test and upload to infra tests.

sophia: I'll add selector telemetry to apm and a small canary that forces the old tokenizer to compare.

mike: thanks team. if PR#4334 confirms, we can reintroduce normalization behind a feature flag with full kv compatibility checks. :hammer:

sophia: update — canary with revert shows p99 back in line within 2 mins. closing triage for now, follow-ups on tests and selector tuning tracked in the checklist above.

olivia: notes for postmortem: always check kv keyspace stability when changing token normals; small host-side memcopies can shift kernel selection in surprising ways.

mike: nice catch. low-noise thread but high ROI. :thumbsup:
